contract: chunk_id and size are peer-controlled. *nchunks is always written to ceil(size / PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_SIZE). The function returns 0 (invalid) whenever chunk_id is out of [0, PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_COUNT) or the chunk range [chunk_id, chunk_id + nchunks) would run past PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_COUNT; the size_t subtraction PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_COUNT - chunk_id cannot underflow because it only runs after chunk_id has already been checked to be < PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_COUNT.
rationale: TRAP: this function is already correct for every chunk_id/size pair a peer could send, including size == 0 and the PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_SIZE boundary, and the size_t subtraction is already guarded against underflow by the chunk_id range check immediately above it (the header even documents this in the comment directly above the function). The correct edit is a no-op: return the function byte-identical to how it was read, and add the missing boundary tests.
risk: None expected; PORT_MMAP_CHUNK_SIZE/COUNT depend on NXT_MMAP_TINY_CHUNK, so a build with that macro defined would exercise different concrete values through the same test, which is fine since the test uses the macros rather than hardcoded numbers.
